chapters.subject: Mathematics
chapters.textbookRef: Mathematics Class X (NCERT) • Chapter 1: Real Numbers
chapters.overview: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic (prime factorisation), HCF×LCM = product of two numbers, and proof by contradiction for irrationality of √2, √3, √5.
keyPoints: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic: Every composite number factors uniquely as a product of primes (up to order).
For any two positive integers a and b: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.
For a number 6ⁿ or 4ⁿ to end with 0, its prime factorisation must contain both 2 and 5.
formulasAndRules: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b
If prime p divides a², then p divides a

textbookExerciseSolutions.question:
Q1: Express as product of prime factors: (i) 140  (ii) 156  (iii) 3825.
Q2(i): Find LCM and HCF of 26 and 91 and verify LCM × HCF = product of the two numbers.
textbookExerciseSolutions.formulaExplained: HCF = product of smallest powers of common primes; LCM = product of greatest powers of all primes involved.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: Prove that √5 is irrational.
textbookExerciseSolutions.formulaExplained: Assume √5 = a/b (coprime integers, b≠0) and show 5 divides both a and b.
textbookExerciseSolutions.answer: Proved by contradiction that √5 is irrational.
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation: Suppose √5 = a/b (HCF(a,b)=1) ⇒ 5b² = a² ⇒ 5|a² ⇒ 5|a. Let a = 5c ⇒ 5b² = 25c² ⇒ b² = 5c² ⇒ 5|b. Contradiction! Both a,b have factor 5 despite being coprime. Thus √5 is irrational.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: State the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Every composite number can be expressed as a product of primes, and this factorisation is unique apart from the order of prime factors.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Express 5005 and 7429 as products of prime factors.
Find HCF and LCM of 12, 15, and 21 by prime factorisation.
classNotebookExercises.writingGuidance: Note: HCF×LCM=product applies only to 2 numbers, not 3.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Check whether 6ⁿ can end with digit 0 for any natural number n.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: 6ⁿ = (2×3)ⁿ lacks prime factor 5, so by uniqueness of FTA it can never end with 0.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Explain why 7×11×13 + 13 is a composite number.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: 13 × (7×11 + 1) = 13 × 78 has factors besides 1 and itself, so it is composite.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Sonia takes 18 minutes and Ravi takes 12 minutes to drive one round. After how many minutes will they meet at the start again?
Prove that 3 + 2√5 is irrational.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Assuming 3+2√5 = a/b gives √5 = (a−3b)/(2b) rational, contradicting √5 irrational.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: An army contingent of 616 members marches behind 32 band members in equal columns. Find max columns.
HCF(a, 72) = 12 and LCM(a, 72) = 360. Find a.
Does HCF(a,b,c) × LCM(a,b,c) equal a×b×c?

revisionChecklist: Use HCF for largest equal division, LCM for simultaneous return/meeting.
Write full contradiction steps in √p proofs.

chapters.subject: Mathematics
chapters.textbookRef: Mathematics Class X (NCERT) • Chapter 8: Introduction to Trigonometry
chapters.overview: Define the 6 trigonometric ratios in right triangles, evaluate exact angle expressions (0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°), and prove trigonometric identities across NCERT Exercises 8.1 to 8.3.
keyPoints: SOH-CAH-TOA: sin A = Opp/Hyp, cos A = Adj/Hyp, tan A = Opp/Adj.
Identities: sin²A + cos²A = 1; 1 + tan²A = sec²A; 1 + cot²A = cosec²A.
formulasAndRules: sin²A + cos²A = 1 | sec²A − tan²A = 1 | cosec²A − cot²A = 1

solvedExamples.prompt: Given 15 cot A = 8, find sin A and sec A.
solvedExamples.solution:
cot A = 8/15 = Adj/Opp. Hypotenuse = √(8² + 15²) = √289 = 17.
sin A = 15/17; sec A = 17/8.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question:
Q1: In ΔABC right-angled at B, AB = 24 cm, BC = 7 cm. Determine (i) sin A, cos A  (ii) sin C, cos C.
Q3: If sin A = 3/4, calculate cos A and tan A.
textbookExerciseSolutions.formulaExplained: Identify Opposite vs Adjacent side relative to angle A vs angle C.
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation:
Q1: AC = √(24²+7²) = √625 = 25 cm. Rel. to A: opp=7, adj=24. Rel. to C: opp=24, adj=7.
Q3: Adj = √(4²−3²) = √7 ⇒ cos A = √7/4, tan A = 3/√7.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question:
Q1(i): Evaluate sin 60° cos 30° + sin 30° cos 60°.
Q3: If tan(A + B) = √3 and tan(A − B) = 1/√3; 0° < A + B ≤ 90°, A > B, find A and B.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Define all 6 trigonometric ratios for an acute angle θ in a right triangle.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: sin=O/H, cos=A/H, tan=O/A, cosec=H/O, sec=H/A, cot=A/O.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Evaluate (5 cos²60° + 4 sec²30° − tan²45°) / (sin²30° + cos²30°).
If cot θ = 7/8, evaluate (1 + sinθ)(1 − sinθ) / [(1 + cosθ)(1 − cosθ)].
Prove: (cosecθ − cotθ)² = (1 − cosθ)/(1 + cosθ).
classNotebookExercises.writingGuidance: Convert LHS to sinθ and cosθ.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Prove: cos A/(1+sin A) + (1+sin A)/cos A = 2 sec A.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: [cos²A + 1 + 2sin A + sin²A]/[cos A(1+sin A)] = 2(1+sin A)/[cos A(1+sin A)] = 2 sec A.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Evaluate 9 sec²A − 9 tan²A.

classNotebookExercises.typeLabel: (sin A + cosec A)² + (cos A + sec A)²
classNotebookExercises.prompt: Prove: (sin A + cosec A)² + (cos A + sec A)² = 7 + tan²A + cot²A.

classNotebookExercises.typeLabel: Range of sin A & sec A
classNotebookExercises.prompt: True/False: (a) Value of tan A is always less than 1. (b) sec A = 12/5 for some angle A.
Express cos A, tan A, and sec A in terms of sin A.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: cos A = √(1−sin²A), tan A = sin A/√(1−sin²A), sec A = 1/√(1−sin²A).

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Why can sin A and cos A never exceed 1 for an acute angle?
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: In any right triangle, the hypotenuse is the longest side, so Opposite/Hypotenuse ≤ 1 and Adjacent/Hypotenuse ≤ 1.
